gloss: The act erects an ecclesiastical circumscription — a diocese, archdiocese, ecclesiastical province, eparchy, ordinariate or prelature.
note: Covers erection only. Elevations (circumscription-elevation) and mergers (circumscription-union) have their own terms; boundary changes are deliberately not included and get a term when evidence for them appears. Populated from the heading text where vatican.va states the act (Francis, Leo XIV: 'Il Santo Padre ha eretto la Diocesi di …'), and from a hand-curated table for Pius XII, John XXIII, Paul VI, John Paul II and Benedict XVI, whose headings print a bare Latin toponym with no marker. See the design spec §4.5.

gloss: The act raises an existing ecclesiastical circumscription in rank — a prefecture to a diocese, a diocese to a metropolitan archdiocese, an exarchate to an eparchy.
note: Covers elevation only. Does not cover erection of a new circumscription (circumscription-erection), mergers (circumscription-union) or boundary changes. Populated from heading text stating the act ('ha elevato …', 'eleva …') guarded by a nearby circumscription noun (diocesi, arcidiocesi, eparchia, arcieparchia, esarcato, prefettura, vicariato), so an unrelated elevation — a parish church or cathedral raised to the rank of Minor Basilica — is not mistagged, and from a hand-curated table for Pius XII, John XXIII, Paul VI, John Paul II and Benedict XVI, whose headings print a bare Latin toponym. Found across Francis, John XXIII and Leo XIV from the heading text. See the design spec §4.5.

gloss: The act unites two or more existing ecclesiastical circumscriptions — whether merging them into one, or joining them aeque principaliter under a single bishop.
note: Covers union only. Does not cover erection (circumscription-erection), elevation in rank (circumscription-elevation), restitution of a suppressed see, boundary revision, or a change of name or title; those are recorded in CANDIDATE_ADJUDICATIONS with the act named, and earn their own terms if further evidence accumulates. Populated from a hand-curated table quoting each document's own argumentum, for Benedict XV, Paul VI and John Paul II. See the design spec §3.
